claim: read() falls back to the legacy location only on NoSuchFileException, but a legacy key whose encoded name exceeds 255 bytes fails the current-location stat with FileSystemException (File name too long), so the legacy file is never tried.
failure_mode: If merged as-is, pre-2.8 complex obs whose titles have about 36+ two-byte (e.g. Cyrillic) characters stop loading after upgrade: AbstractHandler throws UncheckedIOException, TextHandler throws APIException, ImageHandler silently returns no image, where master read them from the legacy location.
evidence: Pre-2.8 naming read at df94143ec (80b4411f8^) AbstractHandler.getOutputFileToWrite: title_uuid.ext in the obs dir. encodeKey (BaseStorageService:110-115) URL-encodes non-ASCII bytes. Throwaway test with storage/complex_obs present: head, 36 Cyrillic letters -> FileSystemException '...%2Etxt: File name too long'; controls 34 letters and ASCII read OK. Same test with master's LocalStorageService: all three read OK. With the suggested read() applied: all read OK, LocalStorageServiceTest (36) and the six handler test classes green; spotless:apply only drops the now-unused NoSuchFileException import. Without storage/complex_obs present the long name read OK (ENOENT on the parent wins), so a regression test must create that directory. Linux: in a python:3.12-alpine container (kernel 5.15) stat on the 259-byte encoded name returns ENAMETOOLONG (control: short missing name -> ENOENT); JDK 21 UnixException.translateToIOException maps only ENOENT to NoSuchFileException and everything else except EACCES/EEXIST to FileSystemException, so read() fails the same way on Linux.
